QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_13

question.text: Grameen Swasthya NPO ran a rural cataract-surgery camp; the programme is co-funded by a Government scheme and other partners in the same area. The SIA Ms. Priya Shah is evaluating attribution. The MOST defensible approach is:

answer.text: Claim 100% of the surgeries as the NPO's attributable impact since it is the direct implementer
Report 50% attribution as a conservative rule of thumb without evidence
Use only CSR-donor-facing narrative numbers and ignore the Government scheme overlap
Consider what would have happened anyway due to partner/Government activity, assess the NPO's contribution, avoid overclaiming, and report the net additional impact using supported assumptions

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports counterfactual and contribution checks and the use of deadweight to avoid overclaiming. Where partner or Government activity could have produced part of the outcome anyway, the SIA must assess the NPO's contribution and report the net additional impact using supported assumptions. The Trap: Claiming all surgeries double-counts the partner contribution. A rule-of-thumb percentage lacks evidence. Hiding the overlap fails the audit-trail requirement. Note: Document the counterfactual logic and contribution assessment in the report so users can see how overclaiming was avoided.
